title: Verb or adjective + preposition
subtitle: worry about, good at, afraid of
summary: Learn which preposition follows common verbs and adjectives, and how the preposition can change the meaning.

lesson.heading: Verb + preposition
lesson.text: Many verbs are always followed by the same preposition. Pay special attention to the ones that are different in your language: learn the verb and the preposition together, as one item.

examples.text: I **agree with** him about the manager's decision.
Many people **spend** a lot of money **on** clothes.

lesson.heading: More verbs + prepositions
rows: She complained to the manager about the food.
I can't concentrate on my work when the radio is playing.
trust it; it will not go wrong
We can rely on this photocopier.
I'm thinking of going to China.
I may go, but it depends on the weather.
His teachers were satisfied with his progress.

lesson.heading: depend on
lesson.text: **Depend on** has more than one meaning. It can mean that something decides the answer, or that you need someone, or that you can trust someone.

examples.text: Martha **depends on** her son for money.
We can **depend on** the others for support.
examples.note: = we can trust them to support us

left.label: to
left.text: **to** = the words or the ball go towards the person in a normal, friendly way.
examples: She **shouted to** me. (= spoke in a loud voice so I could hear)
He **threw** the ball **to** me. (= for me to catch it)

right.label: at
right.text: **at** = the person is angry, or wants to hit you.
examples: He **shouted at** me. (= spoke in a loud voice because he was angry)
He **threw** the ball **at** me. (= in order to hit me)

lesson.heading: Adjective + preposition
lesson.text: Adjectives take prepositions too. Note **similar to** but **different from**, and **good at** but **interested in**.

examples.text: I've never been very **good at** maths.
She's **similar to** her sister, but very **different from** her brother.
I think she's **aware of** the problem.

lesson.heading: More adjectives + prepositions
rows: The neighbours are fond of the children.
bored or a bit angry about
I'm tired of people telling me what to do.
Katya is mad about Brad Pitt.
We're short of coffee at the moment.
There's something wrong with this TV.
keen on / apply for / apologise for
He's keen on tennis. She applied for the job.

lesson.text: When you write down a new verb or adjective in your notebook, always write the preposition with it, plus a short example: *satisfied with (my results)*.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginning of each sentence with the best ending.

pairs.right: to get out of his garden.
his friend on the other side of the lake.

exercises.prompt: *A:* What is she worried ___? *B:* Her exams.
exercises.explanation: Worry about something = be nervous about it.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Who does this bag belong ___? *B:* It's mine.
*A:* What does he spend all his money ___? *B:* Clothes.
He was very angry, so he shouted ___ me.
exercises.explanation: Shout at someone = shout because you are angry. Shout to someone = shout so that they can hear you.

exercises.prompt: He threw the ball ___ me, but I dropped it.
exercises.explanation: Throw something to someone = for them to catch it. Throw it at someone = in order to hit them.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Is she ___ to her sister? *B:* No, they're completely different.
*A:* What's ___ with the radio? *B:* I don't know, but it's not working.
exercises.explanation: There's something wrong with it = it is not working correctly.

exercises.prompt: *A:* What's the matter? *B:* I can't ___ on this with the TV on.
exercises.explanation: Concentrate on something = give all your attention to it.

exercises.prompt: *A:* We're a bit ___ of milk. *B:* OK. I'll buy some when I go out.
exercises.explanation: Short of something = you don't have much of it.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition follows each of these words?

exercises.statement: Max's children still depend of their parents for money.
exercises.explanation: Max's children still depend on their parents for money. We always say depend on.
